title: Org-wide sync: Bridge workshop & cross-team demos — Aug 23 2026
body:
Purpose:
Quick org-wide sync + bridge workshop recap. Share demo notes, highlight cross-team risks, and capture action items that require follow-up across infra, serving runtime, and product. Tone: practical — this is a working doc (notes, TODOs, and unresolved questions included).

Attendees (presenting or on hand): Marcus Nguyen (host), Aisha Patel, Sofia Ramirez, Leo Chen, Priya Das, Nikhil Rao, 6 product and SRE reps, 3 solutions engineers.

Agenda:
- 10m: TL;DR metrics and incident surface
- 20m: Bridge workshop summary (what we tried, demo results)
- 15m: Cross-team dependencies + rollout plan for next canary
- 15m: Open floor / Q&A / action items

Key metrics snapshot (last 48h):
- Total tokens served: ~2.2B/day (hosted + dedicated)
- Average latency (text gen): p50=42ms, p95=118ms, p99=305ms (note: p99 bumped ~20% during eu-west spikes)
- Error rate (5xx) overall: 0.27% (spike to 1.1% during a 30m window on Aug 22, correlated with autoscaler flaps)
- Cache hit rate (KV prefix cache): 62% global; US regions higher (~68%), EU lower (~49%)

Highlights from the bridge workshop (what we validated):
- Goal: test strategy for routing to cheaper quantized variants under load while preserving latency and quality.
- Experiment: live routing policy that prefers 4-bit quantized variant for non-critical routes + optional fallback to fp16 on low-confidence outputs.
- Result: cost/unit token for test route dropped ~24% in steady-state; output-quality regression measured on our smoke prompts stayed within thresholds for 72% of prompts.
- Observed downside: tail latency increased for some sequences when fallback triggered mid-stream due to double-inference; we discussed strategies to avoid mid-request variant switches.
- Demo: end-to-end A/B: 10k requests over 2h — sample artifacts + eval metrics linked above.

Cross-team risks and notes:
- Autoscaler interaction (infra): the dedicated autoscaler triggers new pods slower in eu-west under high burst; combined with mid-request fallback this caused temporary double-inference and the p99 spike. Potential root cause: node provisioning + container start latency + missing pre-warmed buffer for dedicated pools.
- Rollout policy complexity (product/serving): current policy language allows mid-request switching; need a safe default: "no mid-request variant switches" unless request is idempotent/short.
- Observability gaps (observability): lack of token-level trace linking fallback events to specific request IDs in traces makes postmortem reconstruction tedious.
- Cost accounting (finance): routing to quantized variants saved tokens but increased infra churn in the test window — need more conservative cost model for rollout triggers.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Immediate: disable mid-request variant swap by default in the routing engine. Will keep manual opt-in for experiments. (Owner: Marcus Nguyen; ETA: 2026-08-25)
- Observability: add a tracing tag for "variant-fallback" on requests and expose a short dashboard for correlation to p99. (Owner: Leo Chen; ETA: 2026-08-28)
- Autoscaler: infra to add a small pre-warmed buffer for dedicated eu-west pool and tune startup probes to reduce false negative health assessments. (Owner: Nikhil Rao; ETA: 2026-09-01)

Action items (clear owners + rough priority):
- Priya Das: open a formal bug (JIRA) for the double-inference path and attach the sample traces from demo. Include reproduction steps. Due: 2026-08-26.
- Aisha Patel: write a short runbook for rollback scenarios when variant routing causes SLO regressions; include playbook for disabling routing policy per-customer/route. Due: 2026-08-27.
- Leo Chen: instrument "variant-fallback" tag and add a quick dashboard showing p99 vs fallback-rate per region. Due: 2026-08-28.
- Sofia Ramirez: update the model-catalog entry for the quantized variant with expected quality delta and known failure modes. Due: 2026-08-30.
- Marcus Nguyen: schedule follow-up cross-team workshop (infra + product + obs) to review rollout decision tree and update policy DSL. Proposed date: 2026-09-02.

Notes from standups / quick team updates (abridged):
- Serving runtime: rolling restart for canary completed; small mem-leak patched in PR #1412 — monitor next 72h.
- Platform: working on lowering node creation time in eu-west; prototype pre-warm patch running in dev.
- Observability: tracing sampler adjusted to 10% for long-running requests; will increase if we need more traces for debugging.
- SRE / Incidents: current SLO pingbacks show healthy, but escalation path needs explicit contact for cross-region incidents.

Demo takeaways (short):
- When fallback rate <8% the user-visible quality was acceptable and cost savings meaningful.
- When fallback rate rises >15% the tail latency and infra churn negate most savings.
- Concrete threshold suggested: enable quantized routing only when expected fallback <10% and p99 delta <15%.

Open questions / unresolved:
- What SLA guarantees should we attach to customer-level routing opt-ins? (Product wants "best-effort" language, SRE wants explicit SLO guardrails.)
- Should we expose a "safety margin" toggle to customers to trade cost vs latency? (Pros: transparent; Cons: product complexity.)
- Can we compute a better pre-rollout estimator for fallback probability from historical prompts? (Research/ML question; assignable.)

Notes-to-self / informal fragments captured in meeting (do not publish externally):
- Consider a thin proxy that can buffer a short sequence and avoid mid-request swaps without double-inference — prototype idea.
- Talk to cloud provider rep about batch node start metrics for eu-west; gather node boot time percentiles.
- Re-run the demo with larger synthetic diversity of prompts (edge cases that force fallback).

Appendix / artifacts referenced:
- Link to demo eval CSV: (in linked_artifacts)
- Quick script to reproduce local double-inference: scripts/repro/double_infer.sh (internal repo)

Next steps (summary):
1) Disable mid-request variant switches by default (Marcus)
2) Add observability tag + dashboard (Leo)
3) Patch autoscaler / pre-warm in eu-west (Nikhil)
4) Run second bridge demo with broader prompt set and measure fallback behavior (owner: Sofia)

If you see anything missing or incorrect, flag it in the thread (#infra-ops-thread-bridge-aug23) and I will update this doc.

-- Marcus
(quick note: will convert this into a confluence playbook after action items are resolved)
